debatePrompts.title: Lions Led By Donkeys?
debatePrompts.prompt: Debate: Were British generals like Sir Douglas Haig incompetent butchers who threw lives away at the Somme, or did they adapt as best as they could to a new, industrial type of war?

debatePrompts.title: A Truly Global War?
debatePrompts.prompt: Debate: Was World War I truly a 'World' war, or was it just a European civil war that unfairly dragged in colonial subjects from India and Africa against their will?

debatePrompts.title: The Treaty of Versailles
debatePrompts.prompt: Roleplay: You are French Prime Minister Georges Clemenceau in 1919. Explain to Woodrow Wilson why Germany must be utterly crushed, disarmed, and punished financially for the devastation of the war.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: The Spark & The Stampede (1914)

teacher_notes.primer: Introduce the outbreak of WWI, focusing on the assassination in Sarajevo and the alliance system, leading to the massive volunteer movement (Pals' Battalions).

objectives.objective: Understand the short-term and long-term causes of WWI.
objectives.primer: Guide students through the distinction between the trigger event and the underlying alliance structures.
objectives.question: What was the spark that ignited the alliance system?

objectives.objective: Empathize with the young men volunteering in 1914.
objectives.primer: Discuss the 'Pals' Battalions' and why propaganda was so effective.
objectives.question: Why did young men think volunteering was a good idea in 1914?

questions.question: Which of these was a long-term cause of WWI?
options: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
questions.explanation: The alliance system had divided Europe into two armed camps over decades.

lessons.enquiry: Why were young men so desperate to join the slaughter of 1914?

lessons.title: Lesson 3: The Forgotten Empire (The Global War)

teacher_notes.primer: Humanize the contributions and sacrifices of non-white troops from the British Empire, exploring racial barriers.

objectives.objective: Recognize the global nature of the conflict.
objectives.primer: Highlight that over a million Indian, Caribbean, and African troops fought.

objectives.question: How were colonial troops treated differently than British soldiers?

questions.question: What was the main tactical problem at the Battle of the Somme?
options: The artillery barrage failed to destroy the barbed wire.
questions.explanation: The failure of the artillery barrage left troops exposed to machine gun fire.

teacher_notes.primer: Examine how the war transformed daily life in Britain, focusing on government control and women's roles.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: The Fragile Peace (Armistice & Versailles)

teacher_notes.primer: Conclude the unit by analyzing the flawed peace settlement and its long-term consequences for Europe.

objectives.objective: Understand the terms of the Treaty of Versailles.
objectives.primer: Break down the territorial, military, and financial punishments on Germany.
objectives.question: Which term of the Treaty do you think angered Germans the most?

objectives.objective: Evaluate the legacy of the peace.
objectives.primer: Discuss how the treaty laid the groundwork for WWII.
objectives.question: Did the Treaty of Versailles solve the problems of 1914?

questions.question: What was the Defense of the Realm Act (DORA)?
options: A law that gave the British government sweeping powers over daily life.
questions.explanation: DORA allowed the government to censor the press, control pubs, and introduce rationing.

lessons.enquiry: Did the Treaty of Versailles solve the problems of 1914, or create the nightmares of 1939?

Key Concepts: Consequence (the collapse of empires, territorial changes, reparations, and the seeds of WWII).

biographies.name: Yitzhak Rabin
achievements: Chief of Staff of the IDF during the 1967 Six-Day War.
Signed the historic 1993 Oslo Accords with Yasser Arafat.
Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994.
biographies.significance: He transitioned from a military hardliner to a statesman willing to negotiate land for peace, opening the first real path to a two-state solution before his tragic assassination.

biographies.name: Yasser Arafat
biographies.role: Chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO)
achievements: Founded Fatah and led the PLO for decades.
Recognized Israel's right to exist in 1988, shifting the PLO's diplomatic stance.
Signed the 1993 Oslo Accords and became the first President of the Palestinian Authority.
biographies.significance: He was the globally recognized face of the Palestinian nationalist movement, leading the shift from armed struggle to diplomatic negotiations in the 1990s.

biographies.name: Bill Clinton
achievements: Brokered and hosted the signing of the 1993 Oslo Accords.
Hosted the 2000 Camp David Summit in an attempt to reach a final status agreement.
biographies.significance: He was the primary international mediator during the most optimistic phase of the peace process, investing massive American diplomatic capital in resolving the conflict.

biographies.name: Anwar Sadat
achievements: Led Egypt during the 1973 Yom Kippur War.
Became the first Arab leader to officially visit Israel (1977).
Signed the 1978 Camp David Accords, securing peace with Israel.
biographies.significance: His bold decision to break the Arab consensus and negotiate a bilateral peace treaty with Israel fundamentally shifted the military balance in the Middle East.

biographies.name: Menachem Begin
achievements: Former leader of the Irgun paramilitary group.
Signed the 1978 Camp David Accords with Egypt.
biographies.significance: As a right-wing leader, his willingness to return the Sinai Peninsula to Egypt proved that 'land for peace' could work, though his Lebanon policies were highly controversial.

biographies.name: Jimmy Carter
achievements: Championed human rights as a core pillar of US foreign policy.
biographies.significance: His relentless personal mediation at Camp David forced Sadat and Begin to compromise, resulting in the most durable peace treaty in the modern Middle East.

biographies.name: Ariel Sharon
biographies.role: Minister of Defence / Prime Minister of Israel
achievements: Led Israel during the Second Intifada.
Engineered the unilateral disengagement from Gaza in 2005.
biographies.significance: A fiercely controversial military tactician whose aggressive policies deeply shaped Israel's security architecture and settlement strategy.
